# Theory

**Homophily**

Homophily is a concept that addresses the fact that "a contact between
similar people occurs at a higher rate than among dissimilar people"
[@SNASS]. It thus is about if we share similar characteristics, such as
gender or ethnicity, we are more likely to befriend one another. Studies
show that this is also likely to occur on a socioeconomic level, and
that students are more likely to connect with students that have the
same socio-economic status [@ZWIER2023127]. Socioeconomic status is both
about educational level and income-level, but this study solely looks at
parental educational level. We expect that on this level, homophily is
also likely to occur, where students group alongside parental
educational level lines, even when controlling for gender and ethnicity.

*Hypothesis 1:* Reciprocated ties are more likely to exist among
students with parents with the same educational level

**Redirected ties**

That person A sees person B as a friend, does not necessarily have to
mean that person B sees person A as a friend as well. However, one can
imagine that if a friendship is answered, this creates more social
satisfaction than if ties are only sent, but not answered. Therefore, it
is expected that:

*Hypothesis 2:* Reciprocated ties positively affect students' social
satisfaction throughout the year

**Cultural values**

The family one grows up in influences the values one has and what world
one is prepared for. Stephens et al. (2014) show that there is a
difference in how working class families and middle class families
prepare their children for the world, they, in fact, prepare their
children for different types of worlds. First generation students are
often guided by more interdependent motives than continuing-generation
students and these norms remain the same over time in college
[@phillips2020]. Not having to navigate between different cultural
contexts is likely to be less demanding for students, therefore, it is
expected that if students befriend people who have parents with a
similar educational level, they have probably similar expectations in
terms of friendships and it increases their social satisfaction.

*Hypothesis 3*: If reciprocated ties occur between students with parents
with the same educational level, this increases the positive effect of
reciprocated ties on social satisfaction
